title: Fix stdin/stdout pipe deadlock in git helpers and gitleaks runner
summary: Writing child stdin before draining stdout deadlocks once output exceeds the pipe buffer. I add a shared helper in athena-git that writes stdin on a separate thread while collecting output, use it in Git::exit and the gitleaks runner, and fix the xtask policy.rs git() the same way. A regression test pipes over 1 MB through a child that echoes it.

defaults_applied.how: One shared helper fixes the pattern at every call site rather than only the failing test.
Adds a >1 MB echo regression test; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change limited to the three call sites and the helper.
Uses std threads; no new crate.

assumptions: The shared helper lives in athena-git (athena-gate already depends on it); xtask may not depend on athena-git because of the architecture dependency-graph policy test, so it may get a small local fix.
No new crate is needed; std::thread::scope suffices.
Broken-pipe errors on stdin write are tolerated when the child exits, as the child's status is the real signal.

acceptance_criteria.text: Git::exit, the gitleaks runner's run, and the xtask policy.rs git() helper no longer write all stdin before reading stdout; stdin is written on a separate thread (or equivalent concurrent drain).
The athena-git and athena-gate call sites share one helper; xtask uses it or a documented local equivalent if using it would alter the crate dependency graph.
A write error from a child that exits early (broken pipe) is handled without panic or hang.
Run `cargo test` from the repo root: a new test piping more than 1 MB through an echoing child (e.g. cat) passes, and xtask policy tests complete rather than hang.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Other process-spawning code that does not pipe stdin
Reducing the number of tracked files
departures: Slightly higher acceptance because the request is very specific; slightly higher cost for three call sites plus a new test.
